title: Group invitation envelope diverges: canonical-CBOR document instead of COSE_Sign1 Schnorr48 (spec 18.8.2)
description: Spec 12-apps.md 18.8.2: Invitations use COSE_Sign1 (RFC 9052) with Schnorr48-Ed25519 alg -65537, protected header bstr-wrapped 47A1013A00010000, unprotected kid = inviter 8-byte IID, payload CBOR map with integer keys 1-7 (group_id, group_name, mcast, role, expiry, invitee_iid, nonce), signature over SHA256(CBOR(Sig_structure)); invitee validation includes alg check, invitee_iid == own IID, and a per-inviter nonce ledger (ring buffer 32 entries, RAM-only). Classification: divergent. Evidence: Python implements a canonical-CBOR invitation document with string-keyed preimage signing (python/src/lichen/group_membership.py:90-121, python/src/lichen/coap/resources/groups_invite.py:65-115; vectors groups_membership.json) - no COSE envelope, no alg -65537 check, no invitee_iid check at the invite resource, replay ledger is an unbounded per-group identity-hash dict (groups_collection.py:199-214,504-509) instead of a 32-entry nonce ring. The exact COSE machinery exists in each stack for other features (rust/lichen-gateway/src/tunnel_auth.rs:17,511-524; python/src/lichen/crypto/delegation_tokens.py:72-100) and cbor2 confirms 47a1013a00010000 == bstr-wrapped {1:-65537}. Suggested placement: python/src/lichen/coap/resources/groups_invite.py + group_membership.py (adopt COSE_Sign1 envelope, share code with delegation_tokens.py); add invitation COSE vectors; Rust/C invitation handling absent entirely. Refs R-12-062, R-12-063, R-12-064.
close_reason: Re-close (store revert; parent complete: Python spec-18.8.2 divergence resolved — COSE_Sign1 envelope + invitee validation + nonce ring, commits 80ece96798/8402a4d16d; children all closed). Rust/C remainder tracked in l1qw epic tree. See prior close reason.
